claim: NVIDIA Dynamo, a competing disaggregated-inference framework, runs its orchestration layer entirely outside Kubernetes above vLLM, using NIXL for KV transfer, whereas llm-d is Kubernetes-native using standard CRDs and Gateway API.
stance_target: out-of-cluster orchestration for KV-aware routing is an established pattern distinct from llm-d's k8s-native design
scope_conditions: as of March 2026, NVIDIA Dynamo vs llm-d comparison
quoted_support: Unlike NVIDIA Dynamo's disaggregated inference approach, which is an orchestration layer running above vLLM outside Kubernetes, llm-d is a first-class Kubernetes citizen using standard CRDs and the Gateway API Inference Extension.

claim: llm-d has four core components: the llm-d scheduler (cache-aware routing process), the InferencePool CRD (groups decode pods), the InferenceObjective CRD (maps model/LoRA names to backends with traffic weights and criticality labels), and Gateway API Inference Extension integration.
stance_target: component inventory of llm-d as of its CNCF Sandbox acceptance
scope_conditions: llm-d accepted into CNCF Sandbox March 24 2026
quoted_support: Four core components: llm-d scheduler... InferencePool CRD... InferenceObjective CRD... Gateway API Inference Extension integration.

claim: llm-d was donated to CNCF and accepted into the CNCF Sandbox program on March 24, 2026, backed by IBM, Red Hat, Google, CoreWeave, and NVIDIA among others.
stance_target: governance and backing of llm-d as an open-source project
quoted_support: Backed by IBM, Red Hat, Google, CoreWeave, and NVIDIA, among others, the project was donated to CNCF on March 24, 2026 and immediately accepted into the Sandbox program.
